isolation.services: none — pure code inspection and test execution

VAL-GATE-001.evidence: Two dedicated tests in tests/issue-gating.test.ts verify this behavior: (1) 'halts pipeline when evaluator returns blocking issues even with passed:true' — creates a 2-phase pipeline with blocking evaluator issue, user rejects, verifies result.completed===false, phasesCompleted===0, reason contains 'blocking'; (2) 'halts after current phase, does not proceed to next' — 3-phase pipeline with blocking issue on phase 1, verifies spawner.calls.length===1 (only first phase executed) and phasesCompleted===0. Additionally, 'halts pipeline with blocking issues even without approval handler' tests the no-handler case. Source code inspection of execution-loop.ts confirms: after evaluator accepts output, blockingIssues are filtered (severity==='blocking'), and if any exist and approval is not granted, the loop returns {completed:false} with a descriptive reason containing 'blocking'.
testNames: blocking issues halt pipeline > halts pipeline when evaluator returns blocking issues even with passed:true
blocking issues halt pipeline > halts after current phase, does not proceed to next
no approval handler — blocking issues halt without gate > halts pipeline with blocking issues even without approval handler
VAL-GATE-001.observations: All 3 tests pass. The execution loop correctly halts after the current phase when blocking issues are detected, regardless of whether an approval handler is present.

VAL-GATE-002.evidence: Three dedicated tests verify approval gate surfacing: (1) 'calls requestIssueApproval with blocking issues' — verifies MockApprovalHandler.issueApprovalCalls has length 1, issues array has exactly 2 blocking issues with correct descriptions ('Test suite has 3 failures', 'TypeScript errors in src/auth.ts'), and non-blocking issues are filtered out; (2) 'continues pipeline when user approves blocking issues' — verifies result.completed===true and phasesCompleted===2 when user approves; (3) 'halts pipeline when user rejects blocking issues' — verifies result.completed===false and reason contains 'blocking'. Source code inspection of execution-loop.ts confirms: when blockingIssues.length > 0, approvalHandler.requestIssueApproval() is called with only blocking issues. UIApprovalHandler.requestIssueApproval() builds a description string with bullet points for each issue including category and description, then delegates to requestApproval().
testNames: blocking issues surface via approval gate > calls requestIssueApproval with blocking issues
blocking issues surface via approval gate > continues pipeline when user approves blocking issues
blocking issues surface via approval gate > halts pipeline when user rejects blocking issues
VAL-GATE-002.observations: All 3 tests pass. The approval gate receives only blocking issues (non-blocking filtered out), each issue's exact description string is preserved and passed through. User approval decision (true/false) correctly controls pipeline continuation.

VAL-GATE-003.evidence: Two dedicated tests verify non-blocking accumulation: (1) 'appends non-blocking issues to stage context cumulative_issues' — 2-phase pipeline with 2 non-blocking issues in phase 1 and 1 in phase 2, verifies loop.getStageContext().cumulative_issues contains entries for each phase with correct issue counts and description strings; (2) 'pipeline continues normally with only non-blocking issues' — 3-phase pipeline with non-blocking issues on every phase, verifies result.completed===true, phasesCompleted===3, and all 3 spawner calls executed. Source code inspection of execution-loop.ts confirms: non-blocking issues are mapped to _pendingNonBlockingIssues (description strings), then flushed into stage context via accumulatePhaseIntoContext() after each phase completes. Stage context schema (stage-context.ts) has cumulative_issues array with {phase_index, phase_title, issues[]} structure.
testNames: non-blocking issues accumulate in stage context > appends non-blocking issues to stage context cumulative_issues
non-blocking issues accumulate in stage context > pipeline continues normally with only non-blocking issues
VAL-GATE-003.observations: All 2 tests pass. Non-blocking issues are correctly accumulated per-phase in the stage context's cumulative_issues array and the pipeline continues without halting.

VAL-GATE-004.evidence: Two dedicated tests verify normal continuation: (1) 'continues normally when evaluator returns passed:true with empty issues' — 2-phase pipeline where evaluator returns passed:true with issues:[], verifies result.completed===true and phasesCompleted===2; (2) 'continues normally when evaluator returns passed:true with undefined issues (backward compat)' — evaluator returns passed:true with issues:undefined, verifies result.completed===true and phasesCompleted===1. Source code inspection of execution-loop.ts confirms: evaluatorIssues defaults to evalResult.issues ?? [] (line ~380), so undefined issues become empty array. When blockingIssues.length===0, no gating fires and execution continues normally.
testNames: no issues — normal continuation > continues normally when evaluator returns passed:true with empty issues
no issues — normal continuation > continues normally when evaluator returns passed:true with undefined issues (backward compat)
VAL-GATE-004.observations: Both tests pass. Empty issues array and undefined issues field both result in normal pipeline continuation with no gating or approval steps, preserving existing behavior.

VAL-GATE-005.evidence: Three dedicated tests verify independence of pass/fail and issue gating: (1) 'passed:true + blocking issues still halts pipeline' — evaluator returns passed:true with blocking issues, user rejects, verifies result.completed===false and issueApprovalCalls.length===1; (2) 'passed:false triggers revision loop, blocking issues checked only on pass' — evaluator returns passed:false with blocking issues and max_revisions:0, verifies result.completed===false and reason contains 'Evaluation failed' (not 'blocking'), proving that pass/fail check happens BEFORE issue gating; (3) 'mixed blocking and non-blocking: blocking triggers gate, non-blocking accumulate' — evaluator returns passed:true with both blocking and non-blocking issues, user approves blocking, verifies both the approval gate was called with only blocking issues AND non-blocking issues accumulated in stage context. Source code inspection confirms: revision loop runs first (while !evalResult.passed), then issue gating fires separately after evaluation acceptance. The code structure is: revision loop → evaluation pass check → issue gating (blocking filter + approval gate + non-blocking accumulation).
testNames: issue gating independent of pass/fail > passed:true + blocking issues still halts pipeline
issue gating independent of pass/fail > passed:false triggers revision loop, blocking issues checked only on pass
issue gating independent of pass/fail > mixed blocking and non-blocking: blocking triggers gate, non-blocking accumulate
VAL-GATE-005.observations: All 3 tests pass. The two dimensions (pass/fail and issue gating) are demonstrably independent: passed:false triggers revision loop without issue gating, passed:true with blocking issues triggers issue gating without revision loop, and both can coexist.

summary: Tested 5 assertions (VAL-GATE-001 through VAL-GATE-005): all 5 passed. The tests/issue-gating.test.ts file contains 18 comprehensive tests (all passing) that directly cover all 5 assertions plus cross-cutting concerns (VAL-CROSS-001, VAL-CROSS-002, VAL-CROSS-005). The unified-execution-loop.test.ts file (54 tests, all passing) does not contain issue-gating-specific tests but confirms the broader execution loop behavior is intact. Source code inspection of execution-loop.ts, stage-context.ts, approval-handler.ts, and ui-approval-handler.ts confirms the implementation matches the specified behavior.
